title: Room Temperature Sensor Fault
shortDescription: The indoor ambient temperature sensor is open or shorted.
fullDescription:
E1 on Hisense air conditioners indicates the indoor room temperature thermistor is reporting an invalid value. The AC cannot regulate cooling correctly without it.

Unit may continue running but with poor temperature control. Replacement thermistor is inexpensive.

fixSteps.title: Power off
fixSteps.instruction: Unplug or switch off the AC at the breaker.

fixSteps.title: Access board
fixSteps.instruction: Open the front panel to access the control board.

fixSteps.title: Replace thermistor
fixSteps.instruction: Unplug and swap in a new room sensor.

whenToCallPro: If you are uncomfortable opening the unit.
videoSearchQuery: Hisense AC E1 room sensor replace

faq.q: Can I keep using the AC?
faq.a: Short term yes, but temperature won't be accurate.

title: Indoor Coil Sensor Fault
shortDescription: The indoor evaporator coil thermistor is faulty.
fullDescription:
E2 indicates the indoor coil temperature sensor is out of range. This sensor is used to prevent freezing and for defrost control in heat mode.

Replace the sensor to restore normal operation.

fixSteps.title: Locate coil sensor
fixSteps.instruction: Find thermistor clipped to evaporator fins.

faq.a: Without the coil sensor, defrost logic can't engage.

title: Indoor Fan Motor Fault
shortDescription: The indoor blower fan is not reaching the commanded speed.
fullDescription:
E3 means the indoor fan motor feedback is missing or the motor has stalled. Without airflow the AC trips off to prevent coil freeze.

Check for obstructions on the blower wheel, then test the motor.

fixSteps.title: Inspect blower
fixSteps.instruction: Power off and check wheel spins freely.

whenToCallPro: If unit is a split and requires refrigerant-safe handling.
videoSearchQuery: Hisense AC E3 indoor fan motor

faq.q: Why run at all without airflow?
faq.a: The AC won't - it shuts down for safety.

title: EEPROM / Memory Error
shortDescription: The control board memory chip has failed self-check.
fullDescription:
E4 indicates the EEPROM on the main control is unreadable or corrupted. Calibration data cannot be loaded.

On some models the board must be replaced; others support factory reset.

fixSteps.title: Replace board
fixSteps.instruction: Install new main PCB if error persists.

faq.a: Sometimes, but usually board needs replacement.

title: Outdoor Unit Communication Error
shortDescription: The indoor unit cannot communicate with the outdoor unit.
fullDescription:
E5 indicates a communication failure between indoor and outdoor units on split systems. Often caused by wiring faults on the interconnect cable or a failed inverter board.

Check voltage and continuity on the communication conductors.

fixSteps.title: Verify wiring
fixSteps.instruction: Check interconnect cable for continuity and correct terminals.

fixSteps.title: Inspect outdoor PCB
fixSteps.instruction: Look for burnt components or blown fuse.

whenToCallPro: Always recommended for split system diagnosis.
videoSearchQuery: Hisense AC E5 communication error outdoor

faq.a: Only if experienced with line voltage and refrigerant-free work.

title: Outdoor Coil Sensor Fault
shortDescription: Outdoor coil thermistor is out of range.
fullDescription:
E6 indicates a fault with the outdoor coil temperature sensor. This is critical for defrost in heat-pump mode.

Replace the sensor; ensure it is properly clipped to the coil.
symptoms: No heat mode or compressor trip

fixSteps.title: Replace coil sensor
fixSteps.instruction: Swap in new thermistor on condenser coil.

whenToCallPro: If not comfortable opening the outdoor unit.
videoSearchQuery: Hisense AC E6 outdoor coil sensor

faq.a: Mainly heat-pump mode, but can trip cooling too.

title: Mode Conflict (Multi-Zone)
shortDescription: Indoor units requested conflicting modes on a multi-zone system.
fullDescription:
E7 appears on multi-zone Hisense systems when one head requests cool while another requests heat, which is impossible on single-circuit multis.

Set all indoor units to the same mode.

fixSteps.title: Set uniform mode
fixSteps.instruction: Switch all indoor units to the same operating mode.

videoSearchQuery: Hisense multi zone AC E7 mode conflict

faq.q: Can I fix this with app?
faq.a: Yes - set same mode on all zones.

title: High Temperature Protection
shortDescription: Indoor coil or room temperature exceeds safe limit.
fullDescription:
E8 triggers when the indoor coil gets too hot, typically during heat mode with poor airflow or a blocked filter. The unit stops to protect components.

Clean the filter and ensure return-air isn't blocked.

fixSteps.title: Clear vents
fixSteps.instruction: Ensure return and supply paths are open.

videoSearchQuery: Hisense AC E8 high temperature protection

title: Compressor Discharge Sensor Fault
fullDescription:
F1 indicates the compressor discharge pipe temperature sensor is out of range. Without it, the unit cannot protect against compressor overheating.

The outdoor unit will not run until resolved.

fixSteps.title: Service access
fixSteps.instruction: Shut off outdoor disconnect and open cover.

faq.a: Usually not; the sensor protected it.

title: Outdoor Ambient Sensor Fault
fullDescription:
F2 indicates a bad outdoor ambient temperature sensor. The unit needs this reading for defrost and capacity modulation.

Replacement is inexpensive but requires opening the outdoor unit.
whenToCallPro: If unsure about outdoor unit service.

faq.a: Perhaps, but efficiency and defrost will suffer.

title: Outdoor Fan Motor Fault
shortDescription: Condenser fan is not running at commanded speed.
fullDescription:
F3 indicates the outdoor fan motor has stalled or feedback is missing. Without condenser airflow, the system overheats and shuts down.

Check for debris, then test fan and capacitor.

fixSteps.title: Clear debris
fixSteps.instruction: Remove leaves and obstructions from outdoor unit.

fixSteps.title: Replace motor
fixSteps.instruction: Install new fan motor if needed.

whenToCallPro: Usually recommended for outdoor unit work.
videoSearchQuery: Hisense AC F3 outdoor fan motor

faq.a: Yes, heavy debris or ice can stall the fan.

title: IPM (Inverter Module) Protection
shortDescription: The inverter power module detected overcurrent or overtemperature.
fullDescription:
F4 indicates the Intelligent Power Module in the outdoor unit has entered protection. Causes range from high ambient with dirty coil to a failed module or compressor issue.

Professional diagnosis is recommended.

fixSteps.title: Clean coils
fixSteps.instruction: Gently wash outdoor coils and clear debris.

fixSteps.title: Service call
fixSteps.instruction: If F4 persists, have technician check IPM and compressor.

faq.a: IPM board replacement can be costly; sometimes the whole outdoor unit is replaced.
